newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CC-Amatil says did not mislead market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CC-Amatil says did not mislead market.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) managing director Norb Cole said on Tuesday the beverage group had not misled the sharemarket over the timing of its profit warning for the 1996 calendar year.

Australian newspapers reported on Tuesday that the bottling group had told analysts on a trip to its East European operations last month that the group was still on track to meet profit forecasts in the "mid-teens."
Cole told reporters after he delivered a speech to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce that CCA last made a profit prediction in August, when it released its half year results.
"Last time that I am aware that we made any profit projections was ... when we released mid-year results in early August," Cole told reporters.
"At that stage we predicted that the year-end was mid-teens. We have not made any predictions since that time," Cole said.
CCA shares have fallen over 16 percent over the past two days following the profit warning late on Friday.
Cole reiterated that CCA expected "little change" in the 1996 results compared with the 1995 year and would not disclose whether the results would be higher or lower than last year.
He would not comment on 1997 earnings forecasts.
Cole said capital expenditure on operations and the flat retail market were the reasons for the profit warning.

The U.S.-born executive said CCA's parent, The Coca Cola Co, and its other major shareholder, the Kerry Group controlled by Malaysian tycoon Robert Kuok, both understood the current trading situation for CCA.
The Coca Cola Co owns 36.12 percent of CCA, while the Kerry Group through its unit Kerry Beverages owns 9.275 percent.
CCA, the world's second biggest bottler of Coca-Cola, reported a net profit of A$138.6 million in 1995.
CCA shares closed 40 cents or 2.58 percent lower at A$15.10 with over four million shares traded on Tuesday.
Together with Monday's fall of A$2.04, about A$1.3 billion has been wiped off the company's market capitalisation since last Friday following the profit warning.
